notes:
The whole 2.40 series, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on
2.40.0, this is everything since. It is a bigger download than usual.

Restart the console once more after the update installs: tear-free display
then runs only while a game is on screen, so docked menus are smooth again.

The console boots much faster, about 28 seconds to the launcher instead of
about 50. Updates say UPDATING on the boot logo while they unpack, and an
interrupted update no longer breaks the install.

New on Ports and Apps: Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask (Ship of Harkinian
and 2 Ship 2 Harkinian, from your own N64 ROMs, at 20, 30 or 60 FPS, with
mods from the web page), and Mario Kart Wii as a native port (WiiCompiled,
built on the console from your own PAL disc in about an hour plugged in,
with Retro Rewind for online races). Both are set up from the web page's
Ports and Apps tab.

New: a PC Games tab for Windows games, added on the web page: game folders,
GOG installers, disc images and games you own on Steam. Older and lighter
games fit best.

Auto save: in Settings, Display and Sound, Sleep and auto save, RetroArch,
3DS and PS2 games can save a state every few minutes in their own slot. The
controller that presses Launch plays as player 1.

Also: Wii U Call of Duty: Black Ops II starts, Wii U disc keys on the web
page, a GamePad speaker setting and a Capture button that swaps screens;
GameCube stick calibration for pads that rest off centre; both Saturn cores
installed, YabaSanshiro by default; an on-screen keyboard in Morrowind;
docked TVs at 60 Hz; WiFi comes back after docking and sleep; the volume
buttons move one step per press; about 40 MB more free memory.

A security fix: the launcher, emulators and ports now install with standard
permissions, and this update corrects the copies already on the console.
Saves and settings are not touched.

Known: on V1 (Erista) consoles the start of a Mario Kart Wii race runs about
3 fps slower than before, and Retro Rewind's online races were not tested
here.
